answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity carry a mirror of its sponsors' locked stakes: a newcomer joins only when three established agents lock bonds behind it, and a proven fake slashes all three. The second fake from one sponsor costs double, the third four times as much, so a farm's tenth fake costs 512 bonds. A comet audit sweeps the garden each epoch, randomly re-checking identities against fresh outside evidence, and any identity that fails forfeits its stake. Every extra fake costs real, rising, non-parallelizable money.
